examples.purpose: Three options, the guide's Three options card: a period with Daily, Weekly and Monthly. Weekly starts selected (defaultSelectedKey), as in the guide's code for that card. The keys stand for the screen's period values; left uncontrolled, the control moves its own selection when people tap.
examples.jsx:
<SegmentedControl
  items={[
    { key: 'daily', label: 'Daily' },
    { key: 'weekly', label: 'Weekly' },
    { key: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly' },
  ]}
  defaultSelectedKey="weekly"
/>

notes: Extracted 31 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/segmentedcontrol.guide.tsx, self-contained) and docs/evidence/segmentedcontrol.md at 3f56271 (29 October, guide fix #543's wording fix). 3f56271 is on origin/docs-next but not on origin/main (main's last change to the guide is e7ed622, the 27 October publish of #279, #348 and #411 on dbe0e02). git diff origin/main origin/docs-next shows one guide difference, the Anatomy Track note (main: the shape word Coin doesn't have; docs-next: “Rounded lavender background that holds the segments and fills its container.”), plus the same note and the icon line in segmentedcontrol.brief.md; the evidence file is the same on both. So the Track note is not quoted: the Track part rests on the Anatomy description “A lavender track holds the options side by side.”, and every sentence quoted here reads the same on main and docs-next. Versions: the guide's Sources note was checked on 28 October 2026 on 0.1.78 (27 October build), which is v0.1.78-dbe0e02, so /accessibility/0 carries 2026-10-28 and 0.1.78-dbe0e02. Evidence items carry the date and build of the section they quote: the 7 October check (v0.1.78-3795b4c), the 13 October c1fa197 publish, and the 27 October dbe0e02 verification (published 28 October). All are 0.1.78, so the trace check flags none. The 7 October section's sentences that later builds contradict are not quoted (no testID or accessibilityLabel, onSelectionChange firing on every press, no aria-selected, Space doing nothing, wrapping labels, the 269 px row track); only its sentences that still hold on dbe0e02 are: strict-equality selection, the SegmentedControl/Segment override, and its record of the upstream mdx's pointers. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Blobs compared on GitHub (spiefi/coin-components) and with git hash-object in node_modules: src/components/SegmentedControl/SegmentedControl.tsx is 72a73fe at v0.1.77 to v0.1.78-636f3f5, 5340224 at c1fa197 and 5990169, 8716f4c at a116616, 95be09e at ace46ca, 1dc6d4e at c7d3348, 004fd31 at c8526ae and 47598da at dbe0e02 and in node_modules (lib/commonjs SegmentedControl.js e12916b, the same as dbe0e02); its commits since c1fa197 are 8e2a35e, 2214133, 02503ec, 4f2f05f and 928f528, the #279, #348 and #411 fixes. The c1fa197 to dbe0e02 diff is layout only: the track's width (fills a wider column, takes the equal-segment width in a row, at most 100% of its column, a style width wins), a hidden aria-hidden label-measuring copy, and segments with flexGrow 1, flexShrink 1, flexBasis 0 instead of flex 1; selection, keyboard and accessibility code is unchanged. web-platform-utils.ts (e33b52b), JFSThemeProvider.tsx (fa8a86a), figma-variables-resolver.ts (d03e77c), react-utils.ts (bd10632), Coin Variables-variables-full.json (4545aec) and figma-modes.generated.ts (f6aa2f7) are the same at c1fa197 and dbe0e02. So the c1fa197 sentences on keyboard, naming, selection and the callback still hold, and the 27 October sentences describe this build. Every guide and evidence sentence quoted here was read against the installed source (read, not rendered; token values through the package's own getVariableByName in lib/commonjs). SegmentedControl.tsx: items rows are { key, label } (18–21); the control merges JFSThemeProvider modes under its own (225–229); the starting key is useState(defaultSelectedKey ?? items[0]?.key), read once at mount (231–233); handlePress returns when the key is already selected, sets the internal key only when uncontrolled, then calls onSelectionChange (237–246); a segment is selected when item.key === the current key (358), so a key that is no item's leaves none selected; each segment overrides SegmentedControl/Segment with Active or Idle over the passed modes (126–129); a segment is a Pressable with flexGrow 1, flexBasis 0, minWidth 0, 16 × 12 padding and radius 20 (142–153), opacity 0.8 while pressed (169), role tab, accessibilityState selected, accessibilityLabel its label, and on the web aria-selected and tabIndex 0 for the selected one, −1 for the others (170–180); its label is one centred line ending in an ellipsis (155–163, 182); Space selects through useKeyboardNavigation with activationKeys space (165, web-platform-utils.ts 115–141), and Enter through react-native-web 0.21.2's PressResponder, which treats Enter as a press on any role (isValidKeyPress, lines 68–74); on the web the track handles ArrowRight/Down, ArrowLeft/Up (wrapping), Home and End, selecting and focusing the next segment (248–278); the track is a row with segmentedControl/gap 8, background and radius 20, overflow hidden, no padding, maxWidth 100% (280–282, 305–314), as wide as its column when the column is wider than the equal-segment width, else count × (widest label rounded up + 1 + 32) + gaps, so 3 × 96 + 16 = 304 px for Daily, Weekly and Monthly (54–63, 91–113, 291–304); a style width turns that off (106, 294, 368–371), in a row or a column; the tab list carries accessibilityLabel (also aria-label on the web) and testID (345–353). Tokens, Light: track rgb(246, 243, 255), Idle segment transparent with an rgb(12, 13, 16) label, Active rgb(93, 0, 181) with a white label, 16/19 weight 500 JioType Var; at 328 px two segments are 160, three 104, five 59.2 and seven 40 px. No sentence quoted here is contradicted. Tickets, read on the board (read only): #204 (Component Fix, Done, live 13 October): every item it names is fixed on dbe0e02: aria-selected (175–179), Space and the arrow keys select (165, 248–278), only the selected segment is tabbable (178), the tab list takes a name and testID (347–349), pressing the selected segment again doesn't call onSelectionChange (239), labels end in an ellipsis instead of wrapping (182), JFSThemeProvider modes reach it (225). Two points the ticket left outside its Expected list remain: defaultSelectedKey is read only at mount (recorded as behaviour, /configuration/11, not as a gap) and the segment/shadow/* tokens are neither drawn nor removed (141; nothing visible, a token decision, not recorded). Its last item, the stale published Storybook, still holds: the published index (31 October) has Default, Two segments and Interactive, while upstream dbe0e02f has Default, TwoSegments, FiveSegments, Controlled and Uncontrolled, as the Sources note says; not recorded as a Coin gap. #279 (Done, live 27 October), #348 and #411 are fixed on dbe0e02 as the evidence's top section says. #208 (no Dark values for segment/* and segmentedControl/*; Dark resolves the same as Light) is dark mode, kept out of gaps by the pack's rules. So facts.gaps is empty; the evidence's Figma read says the package matches Figma's colours, 43 px height and equal widths. Strength: six quotes hold an absolute word. /useWhen/1 “always in view” (everywhere: every option shows on the track; recommended); /placementAdvice/2 “the track never runs past its column” (everywhere, behaviour, recommended); /configuration/8 “One segment is always selected.” (contextual: while the key names an option, as the guide's own Don't shows); /configuration/11 “read only at mount” (everywhere, behaviour, recommended); /configuration/12 “the control only reports the tap” (contextual: the controlled use In context shows; uncontrolled, the control moves its own selection); /accessibility/0 “the only one in the Tab order” (everywhere, behaviour, recommended). Only /configuration/1 is required, on the items fact (a required prop). The defaultSelectedKey default (the first item's key) backs a recommended rule only. avoidWhen: more than five options (the Squeeze in seven Don't) and a disabled or loading state (States) come from the guide; the guide names no other component, so the Tabs, Segmented Track and Chip Select pointers rest on the evidence's record of the unpublished upstream mdx (7 October), which still says the same at dbe0e02f (lines 24, 84–86, 501–510). FilterBar has no entry in this pack, so /avoidWhen/4 names it only in passing and points to ChipSelect. /avoidWhen/2 (Tabs) sits beside the guide's “a period or a view with three choices”: kept, and flagged by a human flag in reviews/segmentedcontrol.json as a guide question. The Selected segment part is required (always present): one segment is always selected unless the key is not an option, which is the guide's Don't. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every control) and no other modes (the guide's In context Card, control, MoneyValue and Text also set AppearanceBrand Neutral, left out). The first two are the guide's Three options and Five options cards with their own starting keys (weekly and 1Y, guide lines 55–56); the third is the guide's In context card (lines 90–95), controlled, showing the weekly change, with Card.Title, the control and Text as in the guide; its MoneyValue (line 93) has no entry in this pack, so it is left out and not rebuilt with Text. Card has an entry, Text an undocumented one. Left out of examples (three at most): the Two options card (Buy and Sell, in /configuration/3), the Anatomy and Sizing specimens, Tap to choose, the narrow column, Short and parallel, the Don'ts and the playground (its Options and Width switches and Selected readout). Not recorded: style beyond a width (the building rules forbid colour, border, radius and font overrides); Figma's token names, hex values and 393 × 43 frame; the Track note (above); Dark mode; the shadow tokens. The guide's narrow column reads 216 px where the evidence measured 214 px; both give segments of about 66 px, so the sentence holds. Related entries: ChipGroup's /avoidWhen/0 (one choice among options such as Daily, Weekly or Monthly) and /avoidWhen/1 (a mutually exclusive choice points to SegmentedControl, from the same kind of mdx evidence) agree with this entry's use (one choice from a short exclusive set) and with /avoidWhen/4, which sends optional filters to Chip Select, whose entry shows one filter and whether it is applied. Segmented Track's entry is a data bar (nothing pressable; RangeTrack to switch between mixes); its notes leave out its mdx's SegmentedControl pointer, and this entry's /avoidWhen/3 sends a share-of chart there, so the two agree. Tabs and TabItem: neither guide names Segmented Control, and this guide doesn't name Tabs; Tabs' “peer views of the same content” and this guide's “a period or a view with three choices” overlap, which is the human flag (reported to the coordinator as a candidate guide fix). No other guidance file names SegmentedControl. Category input (it filters or switches a value in place, like Chip Select), not navigation. Nothing hand-written here uses the shape word Coin doesn't have; the guide on docs-next and the installed SegmentedControl.tsx don't either, but the guide's Track note on main and the upstream SegmentedControl.mdx (dbe0e02f line 144, “Pill from segmentedControl/background, …”, not in #544's list) do. Cross-check: round 1 raised 1 flag, /examples/2 (the purpose named MoneyValue, which the rendered copy doesn't show); fixed by saying the guide's code uses it, and the reviewer's notes led to /examples/0 and /examples/1 saying their starting keys are the guide code's and /placementAdvice/6 being scoped to a row; round 2 raised 1, /placementAdvice/4 (read as if each label needed about 300 px), fixed, and its note led to /placementAdvice/0 saying “In a column”; round 3 raised none.
